summary: Resumed from handoffs/09 to continue Phase 10 (of 14), the plan's own declared largest phase. Read the full continuation chain and spent this dispatch on design scoping for the origin-tracing extension (Phase 10's remaining task list) rather than on writing new Lean, because the scoping work itself surfaced a new blocker before any invariant construction could safely begin. Confirmed, by direct reading of intApplyRuleFull's exhaustive rule list, that only mint-payload content (T(phi)@w' from an F-rule mint) and the initial branch's starting content are genuine self-origination points requiring new tracking -- alpha/beta decomposition and T-imp-produced content (both reflexive and cross-world) either inherit an existing origin or are already covered by handoff 07's 'case 1' argument without any origin tracking at all. This narrows Phase 10's scope from handoffs 07-09's assumption. However, tracing this narrower scope back to Phase 9's residual x<y<=l sub-case found that origin-tracing alone does not close it: the true self-origination point can itself land strictly between the reuse target x and the reuse source l, recursing into the same open shape rather than resolving it. A concrete worked scenario (a mint-payload world y, direct child of x, whose fresh antecedent later reaches a raw descendant l that reuses x instead of y) shows this is not vacuous, and the gap reduces to the SAME open question already flagged, under the name 'Gap 1', in the pre-existing STOP-gate docstring above IFimpAccess/sat_timp (whether applyPersistenceFixpoint reaches a genuine fixpoint before every subsequent rule step) -- a connection not previously documented. Landing the origin-tracing companion invariant now, before this question is resolved or routed around, risks exactly the 'duplicated churn' the plan's own discipline forbade for ForestComparable, on a much larger invariant. Per the Escalation Protocol, Phase 10 is marked [BLOCKED] rather than landing a sorry'd or vacuous partial construction. Two concrete, non-vague next steps are recorded: (1) a Gate-B2-style computational probe of the concrete scenario (scratch-only, recommended first, cheap relative to the alternative), and (2) a targeted fixpoint-completeness lemma (narrower than DP-5's own 'Gap 1', which would also contribute to DP-5's closure as a side benefit) if the probe does not refute the theorem outright. Also corrected Phase 11's stale [IN PROGRESS] heading marker to [NOT STARTED] (it depends on Phases 9/10 and had not actually begun). Zero Cslib/ writes this dispatch; full regression check via grep confirms the identical 4 in-scope sorries plus the 1 unrelated pre-existing sorry, matching the prior dispatch's baseline (commit 7f9031c0) exactly.
